items.prompt: Starting with fifteen over twenty… …we’ve seen that to write an equivalent fraction with four on the bottom… ▢/4 15/20 …an equation like this one will help us. ▢/4 × ▢/▢ = 15/20 Which has the smaller numbers on the left, and the larger numbers on the right. Next, to make an equivalent fraction, this must have a value of 1. So top and bottom must be the same. Four times five is equal to twenty. So I write five here... and here… ▢/4 × 5/5 = 15/20 Now, finally, I can ask what times five is fifteen?
items.demo: Three times five is fifteen. So I write a three here. *Three fourths* is equivalent to fifteen over twenty.

items.prompt: And if I want a fraction with five on the bottom, that’s equivalent to twenty-four over twenty… ▢/5 24/20 I write this equation to help me. ▢/5 × ▢/▢ = 24/20 Five times what is equal to twenty? Five times four is equal to twenty. So I write four here… and here… ▢/5 × 4/4 = 24/20 Finally, what times four is equal to twenty-four?
items.demo: Six times four is equal to twenty-four. So *six fifths* is equivalent to twenty-four over twenty.

items.prompt: And finally, if I want an equation with three on top that’s equivalent to fifteen over twenty… 3/▢ 15/20 I write this equation to help me. 3/▢ × ▢/▢ = 15/20 Three times what is equal to fifteen? Three times five is equal to fifteen. So I write five here… and here… 3/▢ × 5/5 = 15/20 What times five is equal to twenty?
items.demo: Four times five is equal to twenty. And so, *three fourths* is equivalent to fifteen over twenty.
